hints: Find the driving force of the car from the engine power and speed using $P = F_D \times v$.

Write Newton's second law for the whole system of mass $1700 + 300 = 2000\text{ kg}$ to find the common acceleration $a$: $F_D - R_{\text{car}} - R_{\text{trailer}} = (m_{\text{car}} + m_{\text{trailer}})a$.
Isolate either the trailer ($T - R_{\text{trailer}} = m_{\text{trailer}}a$) or the car ($F_D - R_{\text{car}} - T = m_{\text{car}}a$) to find the tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Find the driving force exerted by the car engine using $P = F_D \times v$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{14000}{20} = 700\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the combined system of mass $1700 + 300 = 2000\text{ kg}$:
$$F_D - R_{\text{car}} - R_{\text{trailer}} = (m_{\text{car}} + m_{\text{trailer}})a$$
$$700 - 400 - 150 = 2000a$$
$$150 = 2000a \implies a = \frac{150}{2000} = \frac{3}{40} = 0.075\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the trailer alone to find the cable tension $T$:
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} = m_{\text{trailer}}a$$
$$T - 150 = 300(0.075)$$
$$T - 150 = 22.5 \implies T = 150 + 22.5 = 172.5\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
First, recall the formula connecting power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Rearrange to find the driving force $F_D$ at the instant when $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{14000}{20} = 700\text{ N}$$

Next, apply Newton's second law to the entire system (car plus trailer). The total mass is:
$$M = 1700 + 300 = 2000\text{ kg}$$

The external forces acting in the direction of motion are the forward driving force $F_D = 700\text{ N}$, the resistance on the car $R_c = 400\text{ N}$, and the resistance on the trailer $R_t = 150\text{ N}$. The internal cable tension $T$ cancels for the combined system:
$$F_D - R_c - R_t = Ma$$
$$700 - 400 - 150 = 2000a$$
$$150 = 2000a$$

Divide both sides by 2000 to determine the acceleration:
$$a = \frac{150}{2000} = \frac{3}{40} = 0.075\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Now isolate the trailer to calculate the tension $T$ in the connecting cable. The mass of the trailer is $m = 300\text{ kg}$, and the forces acting horizontally on it are the forward tension $T$ and the backward resistance of $150\text{ N}$:
$$T - R_t = ma$$
$$T - 150 = 300(0.075)$$

Add 150 to both sides to find $T$:
$$T = 150 + 22.5 = 172.5\text{ N}$$
Thus, the acceleration is $0.075\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and the tension in the cable is $172.5\text{ N}$.
